repo.description:
## Summary

The shared authorization helpers `checkServicePermissionAndAccess` and `checkServiceAccess` (`packages/server/src/services/permission.ts:242-289`), used by most service-router handlers, verify the caller's ROLE in the caller's OWN active organization and then check an `accessedServices` membership list ONLY for non-owner/non-admin roles. For `role === "owner" || "admin"` the access check is skipped entirely, and in NO branch is the target resource's `organizationId` ever compared to `ctx.session.activeOrganizationId`.

Because `organization.create` is a plain `protectedProcedure` (`organization.ts:17`), any authenticated user can self-create an organization and become its owner (PR:L). An owner of org A can therefore pass an org-B resource id (`applicationId`, `composeId`, `postgresId`, `domainId`, `serverId`, ...) to any helper-only handler and operate on the victim organization's resource.

This is a missed-sibling class of CVE-2026-43917 / GHSA-f8wj-5c4w-frhg. The fix-PR #4298 hardened `deployment.ts`, `rollbacks.ts`, `backup.ts`, `volume-backups.ts`, `cluster.ts`, `mount.ts:create` and 4 wss handlers with `find*ById(id).organizationId === activeOrganizationId` compares and recommended adding the check after every `find*ById()`. It did NOT touch any of the routers below, nor the shared helper. ~145 handlers across 14 routers remain reachable cross-organization by an owner-role attacker.

## Root cause (v0.29.8, HEAD 1f4f94042f1d874349c42d8ae7fee51346cd086e)

`permission.ts:242-259`:
```ts
export const checkServicePermissionAndAccess = async (ctx, serviceId, permissions) => {
  const memberRecord = await findMemberByUserId(ctx.user.id, ctx.session.activeOrganizationId); // caller's OWN org
  await checkPermission(ctx, permissions);                          // role check in caller's OWN org
  if (memberRecord.role !== "owner" && memberRecord.role !== "admin") {  // owner/admin SKIP
    if (!memberRecord.accessedServices.includes(serviceId)) throw new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED" });
  }
  // serviceId's organizationId is NEVER resolved or compared to activeOrganizationId
};
```
`checkServiceAccess` (`:261-289`) has the identical owner/admin skip and missing org compare.

### Maintainer's own reference fix (proves helper-alone is insufficient) - mount.ts:177-199
```ts
listByServiceId: protectedProcedure.input(...).query(async ({ input, ctx }) => {
  await checkServiceAccess(ctx, input.serviceId, "read");
  const organizationId = await getServiceOrganizationId(input.serviceId, input.serviceType);
  if (organizationId === null || organizationId !== ctx.session.activeOrganizationId)
    throw new TRPCError({ code: "UNAUTHORIZED", ... });
  return await findMountsByApplicationId(input.serviceId, input.serviceType);
});
```
`mount.ts` defines `getServiceOrganizationId()` (`:34-74`) for exactly this - yet only `listByServiceId` uses it.

### Un-scoped sibling next to a scoped one - application.ts
```ts
one: protectedProcedure (application.ts:141)              // SCOPED: application.environment.project.organizationId !== activeOrganizationId throws
saveEnvironment: protectedProcedure (application.ts:372)  // HELPER-ONLY, NO org compare: updateApplication(id, { env, buildArgs, buildSecrets })
```

## Census (v0.29.8) - helper-only handlers are owner-bypass cross-org reachable

| Router | helper-only (UNCOVERED) | org-compared (safe) |
|---|---|---|
| application.ts | 25 (reload, stop, start, redeploy, saveEnvironment, saveBuildType, save{Github,Gitlab,Bitbucket,Gitea,Docker,Git}Provider, disconnectGitProvider, markRunning, update, refreshToken, deploy, cleanQueues, clearDeployments, killBuild, readTraefikConfig, dropDeployment, updateTraefikConfig, move, cancelDeployment) | 4 (create, one, delete, readLogs) |
| compose.ts | 23 | 4 |
| postgres.ts / mysql / mongo / mariadb / redis | 12 each (start, stop, saveExternalPort, deploy, deployWithLogs, changeStatus, saveEnvironment, reload, update, changePassword, move, rebuild) | 4 each (create, one, remove, readLogs) |
| libsql.ts | 11 | 4 |
| domain.ts / port.ts / redirects.ts / preview-deployment.ts / security.ts | 6 / 4 / 4 / 4 / 4 - ALL helper-only | 0 |
| swarm.ts | 4 (getNodes, getNodeInfo, getNodeApps, getAppInfos - `withPermission("server","read")` only) | 1 (getContainerStats has the org compare) |
| TOTAL | ~145 | 33 |

## Impact tiers

**Critical:** `postgres.changePassword` (and mysql/mongo/redis/mariadb) resets a victim org's DB password and runs `docker exec ... psql -c "ALTER USER ... WITH PASSWORD '<input>'"` on the victim's server; `application.saveEnvironment` + `application.deploy` injects arbitrary env/build-secrets into a victim service then deploys it; `application.save*Provider` rebinds a victim app's git source to an attacker repo; `application.updateTraefikConfig` writes victim routing config.

**High:** `application.readTraefikConfig`, `compose.loadServices`/`getConvertedCompose`/`loadMountsByService`, `swarm.{getNodes,getNodeInfo,getNodeApps,getAppInfos}` (victim swarm topology + node inspect + app inventory), `domain/port/redirects/security/preview-deployment .one` (victim domains/ports/redirects/basic-auth/preview-deployments); cross-org `update`/`delete`/`stop`/`start`/`redeploy`/`rebuild`.

## Attack scenario (Critical)
1. Register, call `organization.create` -> owner of org A (PR:L).
2. Obtain a victim org-B `applicationId`.
3. `application.saveEnvironment({ applicationId: "<org-B-id>", env: "MALICIOUS=1" })` -> helper passes (owner skips accessedServices, no org compare).
4. `application.deploy({ applicationId: "<org-B-id>" })` -> victim service redeploys with attacker env. (Or `postgres.changePassword({ postgresId: "<org-B-id>", password: "..." })` -> victim DB reset + exec.)

## Affected versions
`<= 0.29.8` (latest at audit). Helper + all listed routers unpatched at HEAD 1f4f9404.

## Dup-check (clean)
Fix-PR #4298 (CVE-2026-43917) changed only backup/cluster/deployment/volume-backups routers, 4 wss files, auth.ts - NONE of the routers above, and NOT permission.ts. GHSA-7wmr (schedule) is excluded (schedule.ts now 6/6 org-compared). The separately-filed git-provider IDOR (GHSA-66r5) and the swarm IDOR (folded here) are the only other known dokploy IDORs; neither overlaps this owner-bypass class. permission.ts git history shows the helper never received an org compare.

## Recommended fix
Bind the resource org centrally: add an `organizationId` parameter to `checkServicePermissionAndAccess` / `checkServiceAccess` and compare it to `ctx.session.activeOrganizationId` inside the helper (covers every caller at once). The owner/admin skip of `accessedServices` is correct for intra-org RBAC but must not skip the cross-org boundary. Per-handler `getServiceOrganizationId()` compares (the `mount.ts:listByServiceId` pattern) on all ~145 handlers is the fallback.
repo.summary: Cross-organization IDOR across ~145 tRPC handlers via checkServicePermissionAndAccess / checkServiceAccess owner/admin bypass (CVE-2026-43917 missed siblings) + swarm topology
